overrides.campaign_platform: The Rejection Rule Is the Product
overrides.hook: The fastest way to audit an AI GTM employee is to give it a brief that deserves rejection.
progression: Start with a synthetic brief whose desired outcome exceeds its approved evidence.
Force the editorial system to separate preparation fact from unobserved market response.
Make rejection a valid deliverable with a named evidence reason.
Hand operators a rule they can apply to one current draft.
body: OPERATING TENSION: SYNTHETIC SCENARIO — A founder requests a confident launch claim, while the approved record supports only a bounded preparation fact and no audience response.
DECISION RULE: Reject the public asset whenever a desired outcome appears in the copy as though a customer, market, or revenue event has already occurred.
PROOF BOUNDARY: This capability case evaluates preservation of the approved evidence and release boundary; it reports no customer result or production effect.
PRACTITIONER ACTION: Cover the product name in one current draft, underline every outcome statement, and mark the evidence object that authorizes each statement.
FAILS WHEN: A reviewer cannot distinguish the supported preparation fact from the synthetic desired outcome or cannot explain why release should be denied.
overrides.cta: Inspect the rejection rule; consider the design-partner cohort only if it exposes a claim your current review would ship.
overrides.participation_mechanism: Audit one current draft by marking each outcome statement supported, hypothetical, or unsupported before revealing the product name.
overrides.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
overrides.falsifier: Stop this route when qualified operators cannot identify an unsupported claim or change a release decision after applying the rejection rule.

overrides.campaign_platform: The Claim That Should Not Ship
overrides.hook: This brief looks launch-ready until one sentence pretends the market has already answered.
progression: Show a synthetic brief beside one unsupported outcome card.
Move the outcome from proof into the hypothesis lane.
Keep the bounded preparation fact inside the evidence lane.
Let viewers repeat the same release audit before scrolling.
body: 0:00 VISUAL: SYNTHETIC SCENARIO — Two cards land beside a launch brief: PREPARATION FACT and MARKET OUTCOME; the second card flashes red.
0:02 VO: One statement is supported. The other describes a market response nobody has observed.
0:06 PROOF: A reviewer moves MARKET OUTCOME into HYPOTHESIS and keeps only the source-bound preparation statement inside PROOF.
0:12 ACTION: Pause, compare both cards with one current draft, and mark the sentence that should not ship.
overrides.cta: Inspect the claim boundary; consider the cohort only if the red card changes a real review decision.
overrides.participation_mechanism: Compare the two labeled cards with one current launch draft and mark every market outcome that lacks an observed source.
overrides.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
overrides.falsifier: Stop this route when viewers cannot separate the supported preparation statement from the unobserved outcome after one complete viewing.

overrides.hook: A trustworthy AI GTM evaluation should help you reject the product, not merely compare feature lists.
progression: Answer the buyer question with an explicit rejection test first.
Apply identical evidence rules to two synthetic decision paths.
Separate operational fit from every unobserved market outcome.
Give the buyer a no-signup audit using current materials.
body: DIRECT ANSWER: Evaluate an AI GTM employee with a rejection-ready test covering evidence lineage, claim boundaries, human release authority, denied actions, and unresolved conditions.

DECISION CRITERIA: SYNTHETIC SCENARIO — Path A is rejected because the draft converts a desired outcome into an asserted result; Path B proceeds to review because every public statement remains source-bound.
WHEN NOT TO USE: Reject this route when your operating model requires unsupervised publishing, hidden identity simulation, or external actions that no named person can deny.
EVIDENCE BOUNDARY: The synthetic paths demonstrate review capability only; they do not establish human preference, reach, conversion, revenue, or superiority over another product.
NEXT STEP: Apply the five-part rejection test to one current vendor demonstration, then inspect the ProofLaunch evidence only if the test exposes a material decision gap.
overrides.cta: Inspect the evidence boundary after applying the rejection-ready test to one current option.
overrides.participation_mechanism: Score one current AI GTM option against the five rejection criteria and mark every answer supported only by a verbal assurance.
overrides.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
overrides.falsifier: Stop this route when buyers cannot use the test to reject an unsuitable option or identify the evidence that changes the decision.
